title: Groundnut Soup with Chicken
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: Peanut butter stirred in a tablespoon at a time, then forty-five minutes to an hour on low until the peanut oil separates and rises to the top.
longDesc: Nkatenkwan is the soup fufu was invented for, and the whole thing turns on one endpoint: the peanut oil has to separate and rise. Chicken simmers twenty-five minutes in stock with onion, ginger, garlic and pierced scotch bonnets until the juices run clear, skimming the froth. A blended chalé sauce goes in, then the peanut butter one tablespoon at a time so it dissolves rather than seizes. Then forty-five minutes to an hour on low, stirring regularly, until the oil breaks out on the surface and the meat is falling off the bone.
ingredients: 2 x 850 g packs chicken drumsticks and thighs, skinned
steps: Put the chicken in the pot with the stock, onion, ginger, garlic, pierced scotch bonnets, chilli powder, curry powder, salt and pepper.
Simmer 25 minutes, until the chicken juices run clear, skimming off the froth as it rises.
Meanwhile blend all the chalé sauce ingredients smooth.
Stir the chalé sauce into the pot.
Add the peanut butter one tablespoon at a time, letting each dissolve before the next.
Cook a further 45 minutes to 1 hour over low heat, stirring regularly, until the peanut oil separates and rises to the top.
The result should be a soupy consistency with the meat falling from the bone.
Garnish with the chopped peanuts and spring onions and serve over fufu (GHA001).
chefTips: The oil separating and rising is the endpoint, and every documented groundnut soup agrees on it even where they agree on nothing else. Do not serve it before it happens.
One tablespoon of peanut butter at a time. Dumped in, it clumps and never fully dissolves.
Skim the froth during the first twenty-five minutes. It is what keeps the finished soup clean rather than muddy.
Pierce the scotch bonnets rather than chopping them. You get the aroma and a fraction of the heat, and you can fish them out.
Juices running clear is the chicken cue; falling off the bone is the finished cue. They are forty-five minutes to an hour apart.

Peanut quantity is the single biggest disagreement in this dish — documented versions run from 100 g to a full cup for a comparable pot. This is at the lean end; if you want it thicker, the next one up is GHA014.
Make it up to a day ahead, cool, chill, and reheat slowly with 100 ml of just-boiled water — the author's own instruction, and it genuinely improves.
commonMistakes: Adding the peanut butter all at once.
Chopping the scotch bonnets into the pot.
Rushing the final hour on high heat, which catches the peanut on the base.
sources: Adapted from 'Groundnut soup with chicken', sainsburysmagazine.co.uk. CREDIT AS PRINTED: 'Chef: Zoe Adjonyoh', with a second credit line 'Recipe photograph by Kris Kirkham'. No date is shown. Yield as printed: Serves 6; prep 30 mins, total 1 hr 50 mins. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).

Ingredients exactly as printed: 2 x 850g packs chicken drumsticks and thighs, skinned; 500ml chicken stock or water; 1 onion, finely diced; 5cm piece root ginger, grated; 1 garlic clove, crushed; 1-2 Scotch bonnet chillis, pierced; ½-1 tsp hot chilli powder; 1 tbsp medium curry powder; 2 tsp fine sea salt; 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper; 100-150g good-quality peanut butter; 3 tsp unsalted roasted peanuts, chopped, to garnish; 3 spring onions, sliced, to garnish. Chalé sauce: 1 x 400g tin chopped tomatoes; 2 tbsp tomato purée; 1 onion, roughly chopped; 5cm piece root ginger, grated; 1 red Scotch bonnet chilli, deseeded; ½ tsp crushed dried chilli flakes; 3 garlic cloves.

UNUSUAL UNIT, transcribed as printed and not corrected: '3 tsp' of chopped garnish peanuts. Teaspoons is an odd measure for a chopped nut garnish and may be a misprint for tablespoons — the MelanMag printing of what is substantially the same recipe says '3 tablespoons crushed roasted peanuts'. The discrepancy is recorded; neither figure is altered.

DONENESS CUES, verbatim: simmer the chicken 'for twenty-five minutes until chicken juices run clear, skimming off froth'; then cook 'a further forty-five minutes to one hour over low heat, stirring regularly… until peanut oil separates and rises to top. Result should be soupy consistency with tender meat falling from bone.'
MAKE-AHEAD TIP, verbatim: 'Make up to 1 day ahead. Cool then chill. Reheat slowly with 100ml just-boiled water.'

THE PEANUT QUANTITY DISAGREEMENT ACROSS FIVE DOCUMENTED SOURCES, recorded unreconciled and NOT averaged. Per comparable pot: 100-150 g peanut butter for 2 x 850 g chicken here; 100-200 g for 2 kg chicken in the MelanMag printing (GHA014); ⅔ cup peanut butter for one chicken in the Africa News Cookbook compilation (GHA015); 1 cup peanut butter for 2 lb chicken from Michael W. Twitty (GHA016); 375 ml (1½ cups) groundnut paste to 2 litres of stock from Selassie Atadika (GHA017); and 'about 300g of groundnuts' for a whole chicken in the Mama Juliet version (GHA018). That is roughly a fivefold spread and it is the central unresolved question of this dish.
COOKING TIME AFTER THE PASTE GOES IN, also divergent: 45-60 minutes here and at MelanMag; 45 minutes (Twitty); 30-40 minutes (Atadika); 30 minutes plus a further simmer (Mama Juliet).

THE ONE POINT OF UNIVERSAL AGREEMENT, worth stating because it is rare in this collection: every source gives oil separation as the endpoint, in near-identical words. 'Until oil accumulates' (the KNUST standardised study), 'peanut oil separates and rises' (here), 'oils start to separate' and later 'oils collect on surface' (Mama Juliet), 'until the oil separates and is released from the groundnut paste' (Atadika).

For comparison only and NOT published as a recipe: Appiah CA, Samwini AM, Brown PK, Hayford FEA, Asamoah-Boakye O, 'Proximate composition and serving sizes of selected composite Ghanaian soups', African Journal of Food, Agriculture, Nutrition & Development 20(3):15898-15918, 2020, affiliation KNUST, gives a lab-standardised groundnut soup of 157 g groundnut paste, 305 g fresh tomato, 7 g powdered pepper, 18 g salt, 246 g onion, plus 267 g chicken thigh in its meat variant. Its numbers sum correctly (55 g + 250 g = 305 g tomato). It is a laboratory composite with no stated ethnic origin and 18 g of salt, far above household use.
storage: Up to 1 day ahead per the author; 4 days refrigerated, 3 months frozen.
reheating: Slowly, with 100 ml of just-boiled water stirred in.
healthBenefits: Peanuts supply monounsaturated fat, niacin, folate and vitamin E.
High in protein from both the chicken and the groundnut.
Ginger and garlic both carry documented anti-inflammatory compounds.
culturalNote: Groundnut soup is the Sunday soup — the one that takes two hours and gets eaten with fufu or rice balls while the pot is still on the stove. The insistence on cooking until the oil separates is not aesthetic: cooks across the region treat under-cooked groundnut paste as actively unpleasant to digest, and one named chef says so outright.
